King.summary: Adopted Dec 2, 2025; in effect Feb 18, 2026 outside shoreline areas. Widths are set by stream type; the County says its fish-bearing widths fall within the average range of site-potential tree height.
King.riparian: Fish-bearing 200 ft in rural areas, 180 ft in urban growth areas; Type N 100 ft; Type O 50 ft (was 115–165 / 65 / 25 ft)

places.name: Seattle
places.summary: Update underway; the city last updated its critical areas code in 2017. No draft yet, and an open house is planned for January 2027 (tentative).
places.riparian: Current: 100 ft on creeks with fish or wildlife habitat (shorelines under separate rules)

places.name: Bellevue
places.summary: Adopted Dec 9, 2025; in effect Jan 1, 2026. Widths are set by stream type, with wider buffers where native plant cover is sparse.
places.riparian: Fish-bearing 150 ft, Np 75 ft, Ns 50 ft; 200 / 100 / 67 ft where native cover is sparse and not restored

places.name: Kent
places.summary: Adopted June 16, 2026. Fish-bearing buffers may be reduced by up to 25% with full replanting.
places.riparian: Fish-bearing 150 ft, non-fish 100 ft; 50 ft on industrial valley reaches of Mill, Garrison and Springbrook Creeks

places.name: Renton
places.summary: Adopted Dec 8, 2025. Widths are set by stream type, with wider buffers where native plant cover is sparse and not restored.
places.riparian: Fish-bearing 115 ft, Np 75 ft, Ns 50 ft; 200 / 100 / 67 ft where native cover is sparse and not restored

places.name: Federal Way
places.summary: We found no critical areas update on official pages; the stream buffer rules date to 2015. The state Commerce Department’s September 2026 status list shows the city’s critical areas update as not yet complete.
places.riparian: Current: fish-bearing 100 ft, Np 50 ft, Ns 35 ft

Kitsap.summary: Adopted Oct 14, 2024; in effect Apr 1, 2025. Wider buffers set by stream type; the state agency’s tree-height method is a voluntary option.
Kitsap.riparian: Adopted ordinance: fish-bearing 200 ft (was 150), non-fish 100 ft (was 50), Type O 50 ft; 150 / 75 ft option for some urban projects

Pierce.summary: Adopted Dec 3, 2024 with the County’s periodic update; in effect Feb 1, 2025. Wider buffers set by stream type.
Pierce.riparian: Fish-bearing 175 ft (was 150), Np 115 ft, Ns 100 ft, Type O 65 ft

places.name: Tacoma
places.summary: Adopted July 14, 2026. Widths assume dense native plant cover; where cover is sparse, a project must enhance the buffer under an approved plan.
places.riparian: Fish-bearing 150 ft (was 100–150 ft); non-fish 100 ft (was 25–100 ft); 200 ft on salmon-bearing “streams of local significance” outside shoreline areas (was 150 ft)

Snohomish.summary: Adopted May 14, 2025. In Feb 2026 the state Growth Management Hearings Board sent the stream buffers back for revision by Dec 17, 2026; the County’s draft response widens them.
Snohomish.riparian: Proposed fish-bearing 200 ft (180 ft for some urban projects), non-fish 100 ft (now 150 / 50 ft)

places.name: Everett
places.summary: Adopted Apr 15, 2026; in effect June 1, 2026. One 100-ft standard buffer on fish-bearing and non-fish streams, wider where vegetation is sparse.
places.riparian: 100 ft on fish-bearing and non-fish streams; 150 / 125 ft where vegetation is sparse and not restored (non-fish was 50 ft)

Clark.summary: Critical areas rules were updated in March 2023, using the state agency’s tree-height method for fish-bearing streams. The 20-year plan adopted Oct 13, 2026 leaves them unchanged. The state Commerce Department’s September 2026 status list, issued before that vote, shows the critical areas update as not yet complete.
Clark.riparian: Fish-bearing 150–235 ft and Np 100–155 ft by site class (soil productivity); Ns 100 ft (was 200 / 100 / 75 ft)

places.name: Vancouver
places.summary: Adopted Dec 9, 2024. One width for all stream types, based on tree-height averages.
places.riparian: Adopted 2024: 185 ft on fish-bearing and non-fish streams alike, a 100-ft management area plus an 85-ft outer buffer where development is allowed if it meets performance standards; the state tree-height tool may justify less on constrained sites (was 125–175 ft)

Thurston.summary: Critical areas update underway, separate from the 2045 plan adopted Dec 16, 2025. The Oct 7, 2026 draft replaces stream-type widths with the state agency’s tree-height method.
Thurston.riparian: Proposed: one 200-year site-potential tree height, at least 100 ft (now 100–250 ft by stream type)
Thurston.next: Planning Commission public hearing anticipated Dec 2, 2026

Benton.summary: Draft critical areas code published; Planning Commission hearing held Oct 6, 2026. Raises stream buffers to 100 ft, citing the state fish and wildlife agency’s guidance.
Benton.riparian: Proposed 100 ft on fish-bearing and non-fish streams (shorelines under separate rules)
Benton.next: Commissioners’ hearing Nov 3, 2026, 9 am, Courthouse, Prosser

places.name: Kennewick
places.summary: Adopted Sept 15, 2026. The state fish and wildlife agency had recommended at least 100 ft.

places.name: West Richland
places.summary: Draft critical areas code sets buffers by stream type, with a 15-ft building setback.
places.riparian: Fish-bearing 100 ft, Np 50 ft, Ns 25 ft
places.next: Council resolution to accept the proposed update Oct 20, 2026

places.name: Richland
places.summary: We did not find its critical areas chapter in the city’s draft code package.

Chelan.summary: No critical areas amendments found in the County’s 2026 update; its current rules date to 2021.
Chelan.next: Planning Commission Oct 28; written comments due Nov 3; commissioners’ hearings Nov 10, 2026

places.name: Wenatchee
places.summary: The city’s 2026 package does not include its critical areas title.

Cowlitz.summary: The County’s update page says its critical areas update “is completed with an effective date of December 1st.” Wider stream buffers by stream type.
Cowlitz.riparian: Fish-bearing 180 ft; non-fish 100 ft (25 ft for tiny seasonal channels); was 100 / 50 ft

places.name: Kelso
places.summary: Draft uses the state fish and wildlife agency’s tree-height zones. Planning Commission hearing held Oct 13, 2026.
places.riparian: 25 to 235 ft by stream type and site class (25 ft only on ephemeral non-fish channels)

places.name: Longview
places.summary: Update underway; fish and wildlife buffers flagged for change; no draft posted.
places.riparian: Current: 50 to 200 ft by stream type

Douglas.summary: Draft critical areas code published July 16, 2026; comments closed Sept 25. How the draft sets stream buffer widths is not yet clear to us.
Douglas.next: Joint planning hearing Oct 28; commissioners Dec 8 and 15, 2026 (tentative)

places.name: East Wenatchee
places.summary: Draft critical area code amendments published.
places.next: Joint Planning Commission hearing Oct 28, 2026, 5:30 pm

Franklin.summary: Plan chapters are in Planning Commission review; no critical areas draft found.

places.name: Pasco
places.summary: Critical areas update (file CA2025-005) is at the Planning Commission; we have not yet read its stream buffer widths.

Kittitas.summary: Adopted June 16, 2026. Stream buffers follow the state agency’s tree-height method, set in a 2025 amendment.
Kittitas.riparian: Fish-bearing and Np: one site-potential tree height, at least 100 ft; Ns 100 ft

places.name: Ellensburg
places.summary: The city’s 2026 code package does not amend its critical areas rules.
places.next: Planning Commission hearing Oct 22, 2026; council Nov 2 and 16 (tentative)

Skamania.summary: Joint County and Stevenson draft keeps today’s buffers, with a formal explanation of why it departs from the state agency’s wider guidance. Hearing held Oct 12, 2026.
Skamania.riparian: Fish-bearing 100 ft, Np 50 ft, Ns 25 ft (unchanged)

places.name: Stevenson
places.summary: Plans to adopt the County’s critical areas rules by reference.

Spokane.summary: Draft critical areas code published; the Planning Commission hearing opened July 16 and remains open. Wider flat buffers by stream type.
Spokane.riparian: Proposed fish-bearing 150 ft, non-fish 100 ft (now 100 / 75 / 25 ft)

places.name: Spokane
places.summary: The city plans to update its critical areas rules after its 2026 plan update; no draft yet.
places.riparian: Current: fish-bearing 150–250 ft, non-fish 150 ft (shorelines under separate rules)
places.next: Plan Commission hearing on the plan Nov 2, 2026 (tentative)

places.name: Spokane Valley
places.summary: Draft code (Sept 18, 2026) sets creek-by-creek widths, with an option to use the state tree-height tool where it gives a smaller width.
places.riparian: Chester Creek 115 ft, Saltese Creek 125 ft, 100 ft default (now 150 / 50 / 30 ft)
places.next: Planning Commission hearing Oct 22, 2026, 6 pm, City Hall

Walla Walla.summary: The County’s periodic update is underway; no critical areas draft is posted yet. Its current code already sets creek buffers by named reach, from 35 ft to 100 ft.
Walla Walla.riparian: Current: tiered by reach, 35 / 50 / 75 / 100 ft (County code 18.08.650)
Walla Walla.next: County says plan and code drafts release in fall 2026

places.name: City of Walla Walla
places.summary: Draft raises most creek buffers from 35 ft (50 on Yellowhawk) to 100 ft plus a 15-ft setback. After an Oct 14 hearing, Council asked staff for options no earlier than Nov 4 and by the end of November.
places.riparian: Flat 100 ft on every creek it covers (Mill Creek under shoreline rules)

places.name: College Place
places.summary: The city’s first development-code draft (Aug 18, 2026 workshop) marks no changes to its stream protections.
places.riparian: No change proposed in the first draft

places.name: Waitsburg
places.summary: Draft plan and code went to the state in May 2026. The draft code keeps the existing creek buffers.
places.riparian: Touchet River 25 ft, Coppei Creek 15 ft (draft keeps current)

Yakima.summary: Draft critical areas title (Aug 17, 2026) with wider, tiered buffers; Planning Commission hearings held Aug 26 and Sept 23. Next date not set.
Yakima.riparian: Proposed 150 ft on Type 1–2 streams (200 ft or tree height on salmon, steelhead and cold-water reaches), 100 ft on Type 3, 50 ft on Type 4 (now 100 / 100 / 50 / 25 ft)

places.name: City of Yakima
places.summary: The city’s 2026 package does not include a critical areas update.

Adams.summary: 2027–2047 update underway; no critical areas draft found.

Asotin.summary: No public critical areas update materials found.

Columbia.summary: County draft (part of a joint update with Dayton and Starbuck) reviewed by the Planning Commission Oct 12, 2026. One width for every stream outside shoreline areas; whether it will apply inside Dayton is not yet clear.
Columbia.riparian: Proposed flat 100 ft (now 75–150 ft; 50 ft on small and non-fish streams)
Columbia.next: Planning Commission Nov 9, 2026, 5:30 pm; adoption planned March–June 2027

Ferry.summary: Draft plan and development code posted July 2026.
Ferry.riparian: Draft table: shoreline 150 ft, fish-bearing 100 ft, non-fish 50 ft

Garfield.summary: Joint County and Pomeroy update; no critical areas draft is public yet.

Grant.summary: Update underway with Planning Commission workshops; no critical areas draft found.

Grays Harbor.summary: Draft plan comments closed Sept 15, 2026; no critical areas draft found.

Klickitat.summary: Critical areas update began in 2022; in Nov 2024 the County withdrew its 2022 environmental determination and issued a new one on an updated draft. Current status unclear.

Lincoln.summary: Science review dated Aug 2026; a public draft was expected in October (tentative).

Okanogan.summary: Critical areas update under contract through June 2027; no draft found.

Pacific.summary: Draft critical areas amendments (June and Aug 2026) widen stream buffers; comment period ended.
Pacific.riparian: Proposed fish-bearing 150 ft (from 130), non-fish 100 ft (from 50–65), tree-height option with a 100-ft floor

Stevens.summary: Critical areas update introduced Sept 30, 2026; staff signaled a 100-ft minimum streamside zone. No draft text yet.

Wahkiakum.summary: Draft plan review finished July 2026; no critical areas draft found.

Whitman.summary: Commissioners approved critical areas amendments June 29, 2026; a second round is underway.
Whitman.riparian: Drafts: fish-bearing 180 ft, non-fish 100 ft (up to 180 ft on unstable slopes), tree-height option never below 100 ft; the drafts replace 150–225 ft defaults
